Folks —

I pulled Acme's SAML metadata and sketched a mapping. Key technical points and open questions (quick list):

1) Assertion mapping: Acme's metadata shows groups in the "groups" claim and a persistent external-id on the NameID. We can support group->role mapping via config that accepts either group names or group IDs.

2) Service accounts: For our Private CP, we recommend a pair approach: a long-lived service principal for machine-to-machine (M2M) provisioning (scoped to the tenant) + ephemeral short-lived tokens for runtime operations. Need to confirm whether Acme will manage the M2M principal in their IdP or ask Redwood to host a service identity in the Private CP.

3) SCIM: The attached Acme SCIM doc notes rename semantics as a replace operation (rename => PATCH with operations "replace" on displayName). Our SCIM implementation supports PATCH with add/replace/remove per RFC7643. We should call out that renames trigger a delta sync that may need membership reconciliation.

4) Role granularity: Do they expect per-namespace roles (e.g., per environment) or tenant-wide only? If tenant-wide, mapping is straightforward; per-namespace increases provisioning complexity and will add ~2 days to integration effort.

I uploaded a first-pass identity matrix (rdw-privcp-identity-matrix-v0.1.xlsx) to Drive and will add an example mapping table.

Open items to validate with Acme (for the EOD Wed deliverable):
- Which Okta group(s) correspond to the control-plane admin role?
- Who will host the service principal? (Acme IdP vs Redwood hosted)
- Expected group rename frequency / volume (for SCIM tuning)

Dev
Integration Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachment: rdw-privcp-identity-matrix-v0.1.xlsx (uploaded to Drive)

Thanks Dev — good progress. A few clarifications from our side:

- Okta groups: We have an "RDW-Admins" group that we want mapped to control-plane admin. There are also application-specific groups (e.g., "RDW-Prod-Readers"). We prefer group-name mapping rather than IDs.
- Service principal: Acme prefers to host the M2M service principal in our Okta tenant (okta-svc@acme-payments.com) and perform key rollover on our schedule. We expect Redwood to accept a client-id + rotated secret or certificate for the principal.
- Rename volume: We have infrequent renames (less than 5/month) but bulk membership syncs during org migrations are possible (we’ll flag ahead of time).

James from Okta — can you confirm the best-practice for SCIM PATCH handling with large group membership deltas?

Karen

Hi all —

Short answer: support PATCH semantics and incremental syncs. For large membership deltas, Okta recommends:

- Accept PATCH operations for group membership updates (add/remove) and implement a throttling/backoff for bulk changes to avoid 429s.
- Provide an optional bulk-membership endpoint or accept compressed payloads if you expect large batch imports; otherwise, prefer incremental PATCHes.
- Use the "externalId" attribute to identify groups across renames so SCIM operations are idempotent.

We can work with Dev on a test corpus to validate performance.

James
Principal Solutions Engineer, Okta

Note: forwarded from Okta internal best-practice doc (excerpt)
